definitions.explanation: A round white steamed bun with a savory pork filling. A staple winter snack sold hot at convenience stores in Japan. The Japanese adaptation of Chinese baozi.

examples.japanese: ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肉|にく}まん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a steamed pork bun at the convenience store.

examples.english: I start craving steamed pork buns when winter comes.

examples.english: My standard way of eating piping-hot pork buns is with a dab of mustard.

notes:
Short for {肉|にく}まんじゅう (meat manju). Sold year-round but considered a winter food, kept warm in heated cases by convenience-store registers from autumn through spring.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肉|にく}まん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{蒸|む}す→蒸す：02307_musu⟧: to steam a pork bun
- アツアツ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{肉|にく}まん: piping-hot pork bun
- {肉|にく}まん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦からし→からし：28711_karashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to eat a pork bun with mustard

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦あんまん→あんまん：30279_anman⟧: sweet bean-paste bun — same shape, sweet azuki filling
- ⟦ピザ→ピザ：06769_piza⟧まん: 'pizza bun' — modern variant with tomato-cheese filling
- ⟦カレー→カレー：02898_karee⟧まん: curry bun
- ⟦{中華|ちゅうか}まん→中華まん：30274_chuukaman⟧: general term covering all these steamed buns

REGIONAL NOTE:
In the Kansai region, this is often called {豚|ぶた}まん, where ⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧ traditionally implies beef.
